findings.title: Deleting cache does not invalidate the connectedCalendars query
findings.body: The deleteCacheMutation only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess callback, unlike disconnectMutation which invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars in onSettled. The parent passes onChanged as onSuccess, which is optional and often undefined, and the connectedCalendars query is configured with refetchOnWindowFocus:false. After a successful deletion the dropdown therefore continues to display the old cacheUpdatedAt timestamp and 'Delete cached data' action until some unrelated refetch, making it look as if deletion failed.

findings.title: Cache status includes expired cache entries
findings.body: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groups all CalendarCache rows for the credentials without filtering on expiresAt. The actual cache-read path (getCachedAvailability) treats rows with expiresAt in the past as misses. Expired, unusable cache will therefore be displayed in the UI as current cache with a 'Last updated' time and a delete action, misreporting the real cache status.

findings.title: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache rewrites updatedAt on every SelectedCalendar for the credential
findings.body: updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) is called unconditionally at the end of fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache, touching every SelectedCalendar row (all users' event-type and user-level rows sharing that credentialId, since there is no userId/eventTypeId filter) purely to bump @updatedAt. This adds a write on every cache fill, and destroys the meaning of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as the time the selection itself last changed, which other code selecting updatedAt (e.g. UserWithCalendars) can no longer rely on. The frontend in this PR does not even read SelectedCalendar.updatedAt; it uses CalendarCache.updatedAt via cacheUpdatedAt.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted with the en-US locale
findings.body: The 'last updated' timestamp is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', ...) even though the component already uses useLocale() for translations. Non-English users will see US date/time ordering (e.g. 7/15/25, 4:06 PM) alongside otherwise localized strings, instead of formatting in their configured locale.

findings.title: Tunnel helper script is macOS-only and writes outside the repo from repo root
findings.body: The added dev script uses BSD-only 'sed -i ''' syntax, which GNU sed on Linux interprets as an input filename and fails, and ENV_FILE is hard-coded to ../.env, which only points at the repo .env when invoked from a subdirectory. Run from the repo root it reads/writes an .env outside the repository. This unrelated local-testing script will fail or touch the wrong file for Linux contributors.

findings.title: dev:cron now depends on an undeclared, unpinned tsx fetched via npx
findings.body: The script was changed from ts-node (which is declared in devDependencies) to 'npx tsx', but tsx is not added as a dependency anywhere in this change. Running yarn dev:cron will download an unpinned executable from the registry at runtime, failing offline and introducing an unreviewed supply-chain dependency, instead of using a lockfile-pinned tool.
